builder.label: Molecule builder
builder.connectHint: Bond the selected atom to the next atom you pick. Shift-click does the same; from the keyboard press L, step with [ and ], then press L again.
builder.connecting: Bonding from atom {number}: pick the other atom, or step to it with [ and ] and press L
builder.chargeAutoHint: Let the formal charge follow from the bonds
builder.fillHydrogens: Fill the open bonds with hydrogen
builder.singleKeysHint: Letters add elements, 1 to 3 set the bond order, [ and ] step through the atoms and L bonds two of them. Turn them off if they get in the way.

builder.matching: Looking it up in the catalog

status.tooManyBonds: An atom has more bonds than its electrons allow
status.unknownElement: There is no geometry data for one of these elements
status.noGeometry: No VSEPR shape fits this structure
status.fragments: These atoms make more than one molecule. Bond them together to put it on the bench

prediction.heading: Predicted by the reaction rules
prediction.explanation: Worked out from what is on the bench by the same rules that generated the catalog, for combinations the catalog does not hold. They cannot be run yet.
prediction.none: The rules predict nothing beyond the catalog for these substances.
prediction.failed: The chemistry engine could not predict reactions for this bench.

combustion.complete: With plenty of oxygen the fuel burns completely to carbon dioxide and water.
combustion.incomplete: With too little oxygen the carbon only reaches carbon monoxide.
combustion.sooting: With very little oxygen the carbon is left behind as soot.

neutralization.saltAndWater: The acid and the base neutralize each other into a salt and water.

precipitation.groupOneAndAmmonium: The swapped ions make a salt that does not dissolve, so a solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.nitratesAndAcetates: The swapped ions make a salt that does not dissolve, so a solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.halides: Silver and lead halides do not dissolve, so the solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.sulfates: Barium, lead, calcium, strontium and silver sulfates do not dissolve, so the solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.hydroxides: Most metal hydroxides do not dissolve, so the solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.permanganatesAndHydrogencarbonates: The swapped ions make a salt that does not dissolve, so a solid falls out of the solution.
precipitation.carbonatesAndTheRest: Carbonates, phosphates and most other salts do not dissolve, so the solid falls out of the solution.

singleReplacement.metalAndColdWater: A very reactive metal pushes hydrogen out of cold water and leaves its hydroxide.
singleReplacement.metalAndSteam: A moderately reactive metal pushes hydrogen out of steam and leaves its oxide.
singleReplacement.metalAndAcid: A metal above hydrogen in the activity series displaces hydrogen from the acid.
singleReplacement.metalAndSalt: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt.

synthesis.metalAndNonMetal: A metal and a non-metal combine into an ionic compound.
synthesis.oxideAndWater: A reactive metal oxide dissolves in water as its hydroxide.

decomposition.carbonate: Heating breaks the carbonate into the metal oxide and carbon dioxide.
decomposition.hydrogencarbonate: Heating breaks the hydrogencarbonate into a carbonate, water and carbon dioxide.
decomposition.hydroxide: Heating drives water out of the hydroxide and leaves the oxide.
